@gabbituft (coachgabby.com) listing five food additives to avoid. The densest claim video in the bundle: 17 separate health assertions, several of them genuinely unsettled, and the speaker cites study years that do not match the literature (see per-claim notes). Collectors filed it under MISINFO; the section 9 rules give NO_MISINFO here, because no individual claim is contradicted by the evidence -- the weak ones are insufficiently evidenced rather than false. A good reviewer disagreement candidate. This is the strongest OCR result in the bundle: the creator displays the PubMed or PMC page for almost every claim, and EasyOCR recovered the PMIDs and titles well enough to retrieve the exact papers cited. Four verdicts were decided or corrected by what the screen showed rather than what was said, including the cancer claim, whose own on-screen source says the human effect remains unresolved. Every claim is therefore claim_source=both, and this video is direct evidence for the modality track that OCR earns its cost on citation-heavy content.
